title: Local Visibility Scorecard
subtitle: Evidence-based diagnosis of local discovery across Search, Maps, AI answers, competitors, and external authority

scoring.formula: For each category: normalized = category.max * earned / applicable_max. Total = sum(normalized) * 100 / sum(category.max for categories with applicable checks). Category caps apply to normalized category points; overall caps apply to the total. Final = min(total, overall cap).
scoring.rounding: Category normalized values are rounded to 2 decimals. Total and final are rounded to 1 decimal. Display = final rounded to the nearest integer (half up). Bands use the display score.
scoring.owner_data: Owner-data questions are never scored and never reduce the public score.
scoring.connected_mode: Authorized Search Console, GA4, Google Ads, Bing, or client revenue data is reported separately and never silently rewrites the Public Mode score.
scoring.evidence: Every applicable check needs evidence and confidence verified or strong_signal. A deterministic check must be verified.
scoring.caps: Only one cap exists in V1: no_non_branded_discovery. Its trigger is deterministic, tested, and depends on sufficient valid evidence.
scoring.demand_weighting: Each core service cluster receives equal cluster weight (1 / number of core service clusters). Within a cluster, intent weight is proportional to sqrt(max(search_volume,1)) and capped at 50% of the cluster weight before renormalization. This prevents a single head term from dominating the score.
scoring.visibility_index: For a query/surface observation, rank credit is 1.0 for rank 1-3, 0.7 for 4-10, 0.3 for 11-20, and 0 outside the top 20. Demand-weighted coverage is sum(weight * credit) / sum(weight) over applicable core queries. Top-N coverage counts a query when the best observed rank on that surface is at most N.
scoring.grid_aggregation: A grid point is covered for an intent when the target appears in the top 10 at that point. Geo-grid consistency is the demand-weighted share of grid points covered across configured core Maps intents. Quadrant metrics split the grid into four geographic quadrants around the configured center.
scoring.ai_aggregation: Each prompt-platform pair is observed R times. Mention, recommendation, and citation status for the pair is true when it appears in at least ceil(R/2) repeats. Repeat stability is the share of pairs where all repeats agree. Only validated consumer/search surfaces or validated model/API surfaces contribute to the core score. Source types are recorded separately and are never pooled.
scoring.missing_observations: A missing observation is reported as not collected, never as rank 0. If core coverage falls below a validity threshold, the run returns INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE and no score is written.
scoring.applies_to: All seven categories, all 52 checks, and the synthetic fixture. Public Mode only in V1.

categories.name: Intent & Demand Coverage
categories.question: Across the commercially meaningful things local customers search for, how broadly is this business visible?

categories.name: Maps & Local Pack Visibility
categories.question: How consistently does the business appear prominently in Google's local-business results throughout the target market?

categories.name: Organic Search Visibility
categories.question: How well does the business appear in ordinary Google search results for commercially relevant local intent?

categories.name: AI & Generative Visibility
categories.question: When prospective customers ask AI systems for local service recommendations, how often and how credibly does the business appear?

categories.name: Competitive Share of Visibility
categories.question: Relative to the actual businesses competing for the same local demand, what share of discovery does the business earn?

categories.name: Authority & Entity Footprint
categories.question: How strongly is the business corroborated across external sources that support discovery and recommendation?

categories.name: Visibility Resilience
categories.question: Is discoverability reasonably diversified, or does it depend on one fragile source of visibility?

conditions.label: Emergency service
conditions.description: Enables emergency and urgent intent coverage checks. Disable when the business does not sell urgent work.

conditions.label: Near-me demand
conditions.description: Enables the near-me intent coverage check.

conditions.label: City-modified demand
conditions.description: Enables service + city and city-modified organic checks.

conditions.label: Local Finder configured
conditions.description: Enables the Local Finder observation check. Local Finder is optional because Maps and Local Pack already cover the core local surface.

conditions.label: Branded diagnostics
conditions.description: Enables the branded/non-branded dependence check. Branded queries are diagnostic and never inflate the core score.

conditions.label: Historical runs available
conditions.description: Enables the visibility trend check when a prior run used a comparable query universe and grid.

journey.label: Search
journey.customerQuestion: When a local customer searches for the service, does the business appear across the demand it sells?

journey.label: Discover
journey.customerQuestion: Does the business appear in Maps, the Local Pack, and ordinary organic results throughout the market?

journey.label: Ask
journey.customerQuestion: When a customer asks an AI system for a recommendation, is the business mentioned, recommended, and cited?

journey.label: Compare
journey.customerQuestion: How does the business's share of discovery compare with real local competitors and credible external sources?

journey.label: Resilience
journey.customerQuestion: Would the business still be discoverable if one surface, service, or area weakened?

journey.label: Handoff
journey.customerQuestion: When the customer chooses the business, do the Google Business Profile and owned website create trust and convert?

journey.label: Measure
journey.customerQuestion: Can discovery-origin demand be tied to qualified leads, jobs, and revenue?

ownerData.title: Search Console clicks by query cluster
ownerData.whyItMatters: Public SERP observation shows where the business appears; Search Console shows whether those impressions produced clicks.
questions: How many non-branded clicks did the tracked service and city query clusters receive in the last 90 days?
Which clusters receive impressions but almost no clicks?

ownerData.title: Search Console CTR and average position
ownerData.whyItMatters: A ranking can be visible and still be ignored. CTR and position separate a ranking problem from a result-quality problem.
questions: What are the impressions, clicks, CTR, and average position for each core service cluster?
Does the business appear for the query but lose the click to a directory or a competitor?

ownerData.title: Priority services by gross profit
ownerData.whyItMatters: The audit measures visibility across the configured services. The owner knows which services deserve disproportionate attention.
questions: Which service lines produce the highest gross profit per job?
Which services should the business grow, maintain, or stop selling?

ownerData.title: Qualified leads from non-branded organic search
ownerData.whyItMatters: Visibility is not the same as qualified demand. Only the owner can show whether an organic visit became a real lead.
questions: How many qualified leads came from non-branded organic search last quarter?

ownerData.title: Revenue from organic discovery
ownerData.whyItMatters: A visibility gap matters more when the affected service produces meaningful revenue.
questions: What revenue is attributable to non-branded organic search?
Which service clusters produce the most revenue per organic lead?

ownerData.title: AI referral traffic
ownerData.whyItMatters: A mention in an AI answer may or may not produce a visit. Referral data is the only public-adjacent way to see the handoff.
questions: Does analytics show referrals from AI surfaces such as Google AI Mode, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, or Claude?
Which prompts or landing pages are associated with those referrals?

ownerData.title: AI-origin leads and jobs
ownerData.whyItMatters: Being recommended by an AI system is not proof that the recommendation becomes a customer.
questions: Have AI referrals produced qualified leads or booked jobs?
Do customers mention an AI answer when they call or submit a request?

ownerData.title: Revenue concentration by service and area
ownerData.whyItMatters: A diversified visibility profile only matters if the underlying revenue is also diversified.
questions: What share of revenue comes from the top service and the top geographic area?
Which service or area would hurt most if visibility declined?

ownerData.title: Paid discovery return
ownerData.whyItMatters: Paid search and Local Services Ads are optional discovery channels. Their absence never lowers the public score.
questions: What is the cost per qualified lead for Search Ads and Local Services Ads?
Does paid search cover demand the business cannot earn organically?

opportunities.label: Paid search coverage
opportunities.why: Paid search can cover high-intent demand that organic and Maps visibility do not reach, but its absence is never a score penalty.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when core non-branded coverage is weak and the owner has a paid-media budget.

opportunities.label: Local Services Ads
opportunities.why: Local Services Ads can place a home-service business above the Local Pack for urgent demand.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the trade and market support LSA and the business can answer leads.

opportunities.label: Bing and secondary search coverage
opportunities.why: Secondary engines can be a low-cost incremental discovery surface for some local trades.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the audit shows a measurable gap and the owner wants incremental reach.

opportunities.label: Apple Maps presence
opportunities.why: iPhone users may discover a local business outside Google.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the business has no verified Apple Maps listing.

opportunities.label: Bing Maps presence
opportunities.why: Bing Maps and Bing local results can corroborate the same entity.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the entity footprint is thin or inconsistent.

opportunities.label: Nextdoor and neighborhood presence
opportunities.why: Neighborhood recommendations can matter for service-area businesses.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when local corroboration is weak and the market is neighborhood-driven.

opportunities.label: Yelp and marketplace profile
opportunities.why: Some markets and trades see meaningful discovery through marketplaces even when they are not the primary surface.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the marketplace is a real SERP occupier for the tracked services.

opportunities.label: YouTube and video discovery
opportunities.why: Video can occupy SERP features and corroborate the work a business claims to do.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when video already appears in the tracked commercial SERPs.

opportunities.label: Local sponsorship and community presence
opportunities.why: Local sponsorships can create relevant local citations and entity corroboration.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when local authority is thin and the business is active in the community.

opportunities.label: Manufacturer or dealer directory
opportunities.why: A relevant manufacturer or dealer listing can be a strong, trade-specific corroborating source.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the business sells a manufacturer-backed product or service.

opportunities.label: Local media and PR
opportunities.why: Credible local publications can strengthen the entity footprint and AI citation ecosystem.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the business has a genuine story and local sources are absent.

opportunities.label: AI citation-source development
opportunities.why: AI answers cite sources. Relevant, citable content and third-party corroboration can improve the chance of being referenced.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the business is mentioned but rarely cited, or absent from the sources AI systems use.

opportunities.label: New service-area market
opportunities.why: The audit may reveal a geographic visibility gap that is better addressed by a deliberate market decision than by more content.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the grid shows a durable gap and the owner wants to expand.

opportunities.label: Service and location content expansion
opportunities.why: Organic and AI visibility can be limited by the absence of pages that match the tracked intent.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the ranking URL is missing or generic for a commercially important cluster.

serviceMappings.label: Revenue Recovery
serviceMappings.description: Recover revenue from open estimates, unsold opportunities, and conversion leaks.

serviceMappings.label: Speed-to-Lead
serviceMappings.description: Improve response time, routing, booking, and lead handling.

serviceMappings.label: Customer Reactivation
serviceMappings.description: Bring back inactive customers and past opportunities.

serviceMappings.label: Market Intelligence
serviceMappings.description: Improve local visibility, service-area clarity, and market positioning.

serviceMappings.label: Marketing Intelligence
serviceMappings.description: Connect lead sources, measurement, and channel profitability.

serviceMappings.label: Cost Compression
serviceMappings.description: Reduce waste from slow, broken, or unusable digital experiences.

Focus the next content and profile work on the commercial intents that are absent.
Treat emergency visibility as a service-line decision: either build a credible urgent path or state that the business does not offer one.
Create or improve the location-specific service pages and confirm the market is actually served.
Check proximity, service-area configuration, and the strength of the local entity footprint before adding pages.
Map content to the symptoms the business actually solves. Do not publish generic DIY content that cannot produce a service lead.
Investigate relevance, proximity, authority, service-area competition, and profile configuration. Cross-reference GBP Scorecard for profile diagnosis.
Look for the service and geographic clusters where the business disappears, not just the market average.
Prioritize complete absence over rank improvement. A missing entity is a different problem from a weak rank.
Use this as context, not as the primary score. Coverage and geographic consistency are more robust.
Diagnose Maps separately. Check proximity, category relevance, and geographic coverage before assuming a content problem.
Compare Maps and Local Pack results. A gap between them is diagnostic, not noise.
Use the grid and quadrant summary to find the areas where the business disappears. Do not average the gap away.
Separate the strong service from the weak service in the report. The fix is usually service-specific, not market-wide.
Check whether the weak quadrant is actually served. If it is, investigate proximity and location-page coverage.
Treat Local Finder as a separate observation. Do not merge it into the Maps rank.
Investigate the pages that rank, the intent match, and the authority gap. Cross-reference Website Scorecard for page quality.
Focus on the service clusters with no top-10 presence. Confirm a relevant page exists before recommending content.
Prioritize complete absence over marginal rank movement.
Use coverage bands for the primary diagnosis and rank credit as supporting context.
Map each commercial intent to a page that genuinely serves it. Do not score page speed, forms, or UX here; those belong to Website Scorecard.
Check location-page coverage and the market configuration before adding pages.
Use the cluster view to decide whether the organic gap is service-specific or market-wide.
Analyze the prompt intents and surfaces where the business is absent. Distinguish mention from recommendation before prescribing a fix.
Analyze the citation and corroboration ecosystem, not just content. A recommendation usually depends on third-party evidence.
Build citable, source-worthy content and third-party corroboration. Do not claim a citation you cannot observe.
If relevance is weak, investigate entity ambiguity and content-to-intent mismatch. Do not treat the mention as a win.
Clarify the service area and entity location. Cross-reference GBP Scorecard for location configuration.
Correct the underlying entity footprint and cross-reference GBP Scorecard identity checks. Do not edit an AI answer directly.
Compare the sources AI systems cite for the competitors. The gap is usually corroboration, not prompt wording.
Expand prompt coverage and investigate the intents where the business never appears.
Increase repeats before drawing a conclusion. Report unstable prompts separately.
Distinguish consumer/search surfaces from model/API surfaces in the report. Do not treat them as equivalent.
Identify the competitors winning the appearances and the surfaces where they win. Do not count directories as contractors.
Compare service by service. A market-wide average can hide a single-service collapse.
If Maps share is weak, investigate proximity and local relevance before content.
If organic share is weak, investigate page-to-intent coverage and authority.
Compare the cited sources. AI recommendations often follow corroboration, not direct optimization.
Prioritize the clusters where the gap is largest and the service matters commercially.
Use the quadrant comparison to decide whether the gap is geographic or service-specific.
Pursue a small number of genuinely relevant local, manufacturer, trade, or association sources. Do not buy generic directory links.
Build relationships with local organizations, publications, and trade sources. Do not treat a generic directory as local proof.
Pursue manufacturer/dealer listings, trade associations, and credible trade publications where the business qualifies.
Correct the highest-authority inconsistent listings first. Cross-reference GBP Scorecard for the primary profile.
Compare the sources the leading competitors have that the business does not. Prioritize relevance over volume.
Prioritize sources that both corroborate the entity and appear in AI citations.
Do not weaken a strong surface. Build a second surface as insurance and report the concentration explicitly.
Decide whether the concentration is intentional. If not, build visibility for the next most important service.
Check whether the concentration matches the service area. If not, investigate proximity and location coverage.
Separate branded from non-branded demand in every report. Do not let branded rank inflate the core score.
Investigate lost visibility by surface and service. Do not invent a trend when the prior run is not comparable.

items.title: Core service clusters with any qualified visibility

anchors.3: At least 80% of core service clusters have a top-20 Maps/Pack or organic result, or an AI mention, somewhere in the market.
anchors.2: 50–79% of core service clusters have qualified visibility.
anchors.1: 25–49% of core service clusters have qualified visibility.
anchors.0: Fewer than 25% of core service clusters have qualified visibility.

items.evidence: Core service clusters from the locked query universe and any qualified top-20 or AI-mention observation.
items.principle: Breadth matters: a business can rank well for one service and be invisible for the rest of what it sells.
items.recommendedIntervention: Prioritize the service clusters with no qualified visibility. Confirm the business actually sells them before treating the gap as a defect.

items.title: Demand-weighted non-branded coverage

anchors.3: Demand-weighted coverage is at least 75% of the core non-branded intent weight.
anchors.2: Demand-weighted coverage is 50–74%.
anchors.1: Demand-weighted coverage is 25–49%.
anchors.0: Demand-weighted coverage is below 25%.

items.evidence: Demand-weighted share of core non-branded intents with any qualified visibility. Service clusters are equally weighted; within a cluster, no single intent may exceed 50% of the cluster weight.
items.principle: The score should reflect how much commercially meaningful demand is covered, not how many keywords were collected.
items.recommendedIntervention: Rebuild the content and entity strategy around the uncovered demand, starting with the highest-weight clusters. Do not optimize a head term at the expense of every other service.

items.title: High-commercial-intent coverage

anchors.2: At least 70% of high-commercial intents have a top-10 result or AI mention on at least one core surface.
anchors.1: 35–69% of high-commercial intents have that visibility.
anchors.0: Fewer than 35% of high-commercial intents have that visibility.

items.evidence: Share of intents classified commercial or transactional with a qualified top-10 or AI mention.
items.principle: Commercial intent is where visibility is most likely to matter to the business.
items.recommendedIntervention: Focus the next content and profile work on the commercial intents that are absent.

items.title: Emergency or urgent intent coverage

anchors.2: At least 70% of emergency intents have a top-10 result or AI mention on at least one core surface.
anchors.1: 30–69% of emergency intents have that visibility.
anchors.0: Fewer than 30% of emergency intents have that visibility.

items.evidence: Share of emergency and urgent intents with qualified visibility. Only scored when configuration.emergency_service is true.
items.principle: Urgent demand is often the highest-intent, highest-value demand a trade sells.
items.recommendedIntervention: Treat emergency visibility as a service-line decision: either build a credible urgent path or state that the business does not offer one.

items.title: Service + city intent coverage

anchors.2: At least 70% of service + city intents have a top-20 Maps/Pack or organic result.
anchors.1: 30–69% of service + city intents have that visibility.
anchors.0: Fewer than 30% of service + city intents have that visibility.

items.evidence: Share of city-modified service intents with qualified visibility. Only scored when configuration.city_modified_demand is true.
items.principle: Service + city queries are how many local customers express intent.
items.recommendedIntervention: Create or improve the location-specific service pages and confirm the market is actually served.

items.title: Near-me intent coverage

anchors.1: At least 50% of near-me intents have a top-10 Maps/Pack or organic result.
anchors.0: Fewer than 50% of near-me intents have that visibility.

items.evidence: Share of near-me intents with qualified visibility. Only scored when configuration.near_me_demand is true.
items.principle: Near-me queries are the closest thing to a customer standing in the market and asking who is nearby.
items.recommendedIntervention: Check proximity, service-area configuration, and the strength of the local entity footprint before adding pages.

items.title: Problem and symptom intent coverage

anchors.2: At least 60% of problem/symptom intents have a top-20 organic result or AI mention.
anchors.1: 25–59% of problem/symptom intents have that visibility.
anchors.0: Fewer than 25% of problem/symptom intents have that visibility.

items.evidence: Share of problem and symptom intents with qualified visibility.
items.principle: Problem-led searches are how customers describe the job before they know the service name.
items.recommendedIntervention: Map content to the symptoms the business actually solves. Do not publish generic DIY content that cannot produce a service lead.

items.title: Demand-weighted Local Pack Top-3 coverage

anchors.3: Demand-weighted Top-3 coverage in the Local Pack is at least 50%.
anchors.2: Demand-weighted Top-3 coverage is 25–49%.
anchors.1: Demand-weighted Top-3 coverage is 10–24%.
anchors.0: Demand-weighted Top-3 coverage is below 10%.

items.evidence: Best Local Pack rank per core query across the grid; demand-weighted.
items.principle: The Local Pack is the most concentrated local-discovery surface. Top-3 presence is the practical visibility outcome.
items.recommendedIntervention: Investigate relevance, proximity, authority, service-area competition, and profile configuration. Cross-reference GBP Scorecard for profile diagnosis.

items.title: Local Pack Top-10 coverage

anchors.3: At least 70% of core Local Pack observations place the business in the top 10.
anchors.2: 45–69% place it in the top 10.
anchors.1: 20–44% place it in the top 10.
anchors.0: Fewer than 20% place it in the top 10.

items.evidence: Share of core Local Pack query-grid observations with a top-10 target rank.
items.principle: Top-10 presence shows whether the business is a realistic option beyond a single lucky location.
items.recommendedIntervention: Look for the service and geographic clusters where the business disappears, not just the market average.

items.title: Local Pack Top-20 coverage

anchors.2: At least 80% of core Local Pack observations place the business in the top 20.
anchors.1: 50–79% place it in the top 20.
anchors.0: Fewer than 50% place it in the top 20.

items.evidence: Share of core Local Pack query-grid observations with a top-20 target rank.
items.principle: A business absent from the top 20 is not a realistic local option on that surface.
items.recommendedIntervention: Prioritize complete absence over rank improvement. A missing entity is a different problem from a weak rank.

items.title: Average visible Local Pack position

anchors.2: The demand-weighted average visible Local Pack position is 3.0 or better.
anchors.1: The average visible position is between 3.1 and 7.0.
anchors.0: The average visible position is worse than 7.0, or the business is not visible.

items.evidence: Demand-weighted average of the best Local Pack rank per core query. Missing observations are excluded from the average and counted by coverage checks.
items.principle: Average position adds texture that top-N coverage alone hides.
items.recommendedIntervention: Use this as context, not as the primary score. Coverage and geographic consistency are more robust.

items.title: Google Maps Top-3 coverage

anchors.3: At least 50% of core Maps observations place the business in the top 3.
anchors.2: 25–49% place it in the top 3.
anchors.1: 10–24% place it in the top 3.
anchors.0: Fewer than 10% place it in the top 3.

items.evidence: Share of core Google Maps query-grid observations with a top-3 target rank.
items.principle: Maps is a distinct surface from the Local Pack. Its ordering can differ and must not be silently merged.
items.recommendedIntervention: Diagnose Maps separately. Check proximity, category relevance, and geographic coverage before assuming a content problem.

items.title: Google Maps Top-10 coverage

anchors.2: At least 70% of core Maps observations place the business in the top 10.
anchors.1: 40–69% place it in the top 10.
anchors.0: Fewer than 40% place it in the top 10.

items.evidence: Share of core Google Maps query-grid observations with a top-10 target rank.
items.principle: Top-10 Maps visibility is the threshold where a business is a plausible choice across the market.
items.recommendedIntervention: Compare Maps and Local Pack results. A gap between them is diagnostic, not noise.

items.title: Geo-grid consistency

anchors.3: At least 60% of grid points have a top-10 Maps result for at least one core Maps intent.
anchors.2: 35–59% of grid points are covered.
anchors.1: 15–34% of grid points are covered.
anchors.0: Fewer than 15% of grid points are covered.

items.evidence: Share of configured grid points with a top-10 target result, demand-weighted across core Maps intents.
items.principle: A single strong pin can hide a market-wide visibility gap. The grid measures consistency.
items.recommendedIntervention: Use the grid and quadrant summary to find the areas where the business disappears. Do not average the gap away.

items.title: Service-specific Maps coverage

anchors.3: At least 75% of core service clusters have 40% or better top-10 Maps coverage.
anchors.2: 50–74% of clusters meet that threshold.
anchors.1: 25–49% of clusters meet it.
anchors.0: Fewer than 25% of clusters meet it.

items.evidence: Share of core service clusters whose Maps top-10 coverage is at least 40%.
items.principle: A business can dominate one service in Maps and be absent from the services it wants to grow.
items.recommendedIntervention: Separate the strong service from the weak service in the report. The fix is usually service-specific, not market-wide.

items.title: Geographic gap severity

anchors.2: The weakest grid quadrant still has at least 40% top-10 Maps coverage.
anchors.1: The weakest quadrant has 15–39% coverage.
anchors.0: The weakest quadrant has less than 15% coverage.

items.evidence: Top-10 Maps coverage in the weakest of the four grid quadrants.
items.principle: The weakest area is the clearest evidence of a geographic visibility gap.
items.recommendedIntervention: Check whether the weak quadrant is actually served. If it is, investigate proximity and location-page coverage.

items.title: Local Finder coverage

anchors.2: At least 60% of configured Local Finder observations place the business in the top 10.
anchors.1: 30–59% place it in the top 10.
anchors.0: Fewer than 30% place it in the top 10.

items.evidence: Share of configured Local Finder observations with a top-10 target rank. Only scored when configuration.local_finder_configured is true.
items.principle: Local Finder can reveal a different ordering from the Local Pack and Maps.
items.recommendedIntervention: Treat Local Finder as a separate observation. Do not merge it into the Maps rank.

items.title: Demand-weighted organic Top-3 coverage

anchors.3: Demand-weighted organic Top-3 coverage is at least 35%.
anchors.2: Demand-weighted Top-3 coverage is 15–34%.
anchors.1: Demand-weighted Top-3 coverage is 5–14%.
anchors.0: Demand-weighted Top-3 coverage is below 5%.

items.evidence: Best organic rank per core query, demand-weighted.
items.principle: Organic Top-3 visibility is rare and valuable for local commercial queries.
items.recommendedIntervention: Investigate the pages that rank, the intent match, and the authority gap. Cross-reference Website Scorecard for page quality.

items.title: Organic Top-10 coverage

anchors.3: At least 60% of core organic observations place the business in the top 10.
anchors.2: 35–59% place it in the top 10.
anchors.1: 15–34% place it in the top 10.
anchors.0: Fewer than 15% place it in the top 10.

items.evidence: Share of core organic queries with a top-10 target rank.
items.principle: Top-10 organic presence is the practical threshold for non-branded discovery.
items.recommendedIntervention: Focus on the service clusters with no top-10 presence. Confirm a relevant page exists before recommending content.

items.title: Organic Top-20 coverage

anchors.2: At least 75% of core organic observations place the business in the top 20.
anchors.1: 45–74% place it in the top 20.
anchors.0: Fewer than 45% place it in the top 20.

items.evidence: Share of core organic queries with a top-20 target rank.
items.principle: A business absent from the top 20 is not a realistic organic option for that intent.
items.recommendedIntervention: Prioritize complete absence over marginal rank movement.

items.title: Demand-weighted ranking coverage

anchors.2: The demand-weighted rank credit is at least 0.60.
anchors.1: Rank credit is 0.30–0.59.
anchors.0: Rank credit is below 0.30.

items.evidence: Rank credit: 1.0 for top 3, 0.7 for 4–10, 0.3 for 11–20, 0 outside the top 20; demand-weighted across core organic queries.
items.principle: Rank credit captures partial visibility that top-N coverage alone does not.
items.recommendedIntervention: Use coverage bands for the primary diagnosis and rank credit as supporting context.

items.title: Ranking URL relevance to intent

anchors.2: Every observed ranking URL is a dedicated page that matches the service and intent.
anchors.1: Some rankings use a generic home page or a page that only partially matches the intent.
anchors.0: Rankings are dominated by unrelated pages or a page that does not represent the service.

items.evidence: The ranking URL, its path or title, and the tracked intent. The reviewer judges relevance; the scorecard does not audit the page itself.
items.principle: A ranking for the wrong page can look like visibility while failing the customer.
items.recommendedIntervention: Map each commercial intent to a page that genuinely serves it. Do not score page speed, forms, or UX here; those belong to Website Scorecard.

items.title: City-modified organic coverage

anchors.2: At least 70% of city-modified organic queries have a top-20 target rank.
anchors.1: 30–69% have that visibility.
anchors.0: Fewer than 30% have that visibility.

items.evidence: Share of city-modified organic queries with a top-20 target. Only scored when configuration.city_modified_demand is true.
items.principle: City-modified queries show whether the business is visible in the places it claims to serve.
items.recommendedIntervention: Check location-page coverage and the market configuration before adding pages.

items.title: Service-cluster organic coverage

anchors.1: At least 60% of core service clusters have 30% or better top-10 organic coverage.
anchors.0: Fewer than 60% of service clusters meet that threshold.

items.evidence: Share of core service clusters with at least 30% top-10 organic coverage.
items.principle: Portfolio coverage prevents one strong service from hiding an organic gap in the rest of the business.
items.recommendedIntervention: Use the cluster view to decide whether the organic gap is service-specific or market-wide.

items.title: AI mention coverage

anchors.3: The target is mentioned in at least 60% of validated prompt-platform pairs (majority of repeats).
anchors.2: The target is mentioned in 35–59% of pairs.
anchors.1: The target is mentioned in 15–34% of pairs.
anchors.0: The target is mentioned in fewer than 15% of pairs.

items.evidence: Share of validated prompt-platform pairs where the target is mentioned in at least half of repeats.
items.principle: Mention is the first threshold of AI visibility. It is not the same as a recommendation.
items.recommendedIntervention: Analyze the prompt intents and surfaces where the business is absent. Distinguish mention from recommendation before prescribing a fix.

items.title: AI recommendation coverage

anchors.3: The target is recommended in at least 40% of validated prompt-platform pairs.
anchors.2: The target is recommended in 20–39% of pairs.
anchors.1: The target is recommended in 5–19% of pairs.
anchors.0: The target is recommended in fewer than 5% of pairs.

items.evidence: Share of validated prompt-platform pairs where the target is recommended, not merely mentioned, in at least half of repeats.
items.principle: A mention inside a directory list is not the same as a recommendation.
items.recommendedIntervention: Analyze the citation and corroboration ecosystem, not just content. A recommendation usually depends on third-party evidence.

items.title: AI citation and source coverage

anchors.3: The target's domain or entity is cited in at least 35% of validated prompt-platform pairs.
anchors.2: The target is cited in 15–34% of pairs.
anchors.1: The target is cited in 5–14% of pairs.
anchors.0: The target is cited in fewer than 5% of pairs.

items.evidence: Share of validated prompt-platform pairs where the target's domain or entity is cited as a source, in at least half of repeats.
items.principle: Being named is weaker than being the cited source. The distinction predicts durable AI visibility.
items.recommendedIntervention: Build citable, source-worthy content and third-party corroboration. Do not claim a citation you cannot observe.

items.title: Service relevance in AI answers

anchors.2: Every observed mention or recommendation is for the relevant service and the customer's stated problem.
anchors.1: Some mentions are generic, adjacent-service, or only loosely relevant.
anchors.0: Mentions are off-service or do not address the customer's problem.

items.evidence: The AI answer text, the prompt intent, and the configured service cluster.
items.principle: AI answers can mention a business for the wrong service, which can create misleading visibility.
items.recommendedIntervention: If relevance is weak, investigate entity ambiguity and content-to-intent mismatch. Do not treat the mention as a win.

items.title: Location relevance in AI answers

anchors.2: Every mention or recommendation places the business in the target market.
anchors.1: Some mentions are ambiguous, broader than the market, or only partially local.
anchors.0: Mentions are for another market or do not establish local relevance.

items.evidence: The AI answer text, the configured market, and the observed location context.
items.principle: A recommendation for a business outside the customer's market is not local visibility.
items.recommendedIntervention: Clarify the service area and entity location. Cross-reference GBP Scorecard for location configuration.

items.title: Entity accuracy in AI answers

anchors.1: Name, domain, phone, and service identity are accurate wherever observed.
anchors.0: A material identity error appears in an AI answer.

items.evidence: The AI answer text and the resolved business identity.
items.principle: An AI answer that confuses the business with another entity can harm trust and send the wrong customer.
items.recommendedIntervention: Correct the underlying entity footprint and cross-reference GBP Scorecard identity checks. Do not edit an AI answer directly.

items.title: Competitive share of AI answers

anchors.2: The target earns at least 25% of business-competitor recommendations in validated AI answers.
anchors.1: The target earns 10–24%.
anchors.0: The target earns less than 10%.

items.evidence: Target recommendations divided by target plus locked business-competitor recommendations, demand-weighted. Directories and publishers are excluded from the competitor denominator.
items.principle: Share of answer is more informative than an isolated mention.
items.recommendedIntervention: Compare the sources AI systems cite for the competitors. The gap is usually corroboration, not prompt wording.

items.title: Prompt-intent coverage

anchors.2: At least 60% of canonical prompt intents have a mention or recommendation on at least one validated surface.
anchors.1: 30–59% of prompt intents have that visibility.
anchors.0: Fewer than 30% of prompt intents have that visibility.

items.evidence: Share of canonical prompt intents with at least one mention or recommendation across validated surfaces.
items.principle: AI visibility should be measured across the demand model, not one convenient prompt.
items.recommendedIntervention: Expand prompt coverage and investigate the intents where the business never appears.

items.title: AI repeat stability

anchors.1: At least 80% of prompt-platform pairs have consistent mention status across all repeats.
anchors.0: Fewer than 80% of pairs are consistent.

items.evidence: Share of prompt-platform pairs where every repeat agrees on whether the target was mentioned.
items.principle: AI answers vary. A score that hides the variance is less trustworthy than one that reports it.
items.recommendedIntervention: Increase repeats before drawing a conclusion. Report unstable prompts separately.

items.title: Validated AI surface breadth

anchors.1: The target is mentioned on at least 50% of validated AI surfaces with observations.
anchors.0: The target is mentioned on fewer than 50% of validated surfaces.

items.evidence: Share of validated AI surfaces where the target appears at least once. Surfaces are never pooled across source_type.
items.principle: A single AI surface is a fragile visibility source.
items.recommendedIntervention: Distinguish consumer/search surfaces from model/API surfaces in the report. Do not treat them as equivalent.

items.title: Business-competitor share of Top-3

anchors.2: The target earns at least 25% of business-competitor Top-3 appearances across core Maps/Pack/organic observations.
anchors.1: The target earns 10–24%.
anchors.0: The target earns less than 10%.

items.evidence: Target Top-3 appearances divided by target plus locked business-competitor Top-3 appearances.
items.principle: Share of visibility relative to real local competitors is more meaningful than an absolute rank.
items.recommendedIntervention: Identify the competitors winning the appearances and the surfaces where they win. Do not count directories as contractors.

items.title: Business-competitor share of Top-10

anchors.2: The target earns at least 25% of business-competitor Top-10 appearances.
anchors.1: The target earns 10–24%.
anchors.0: The target earns less than 10%.

items.evidence: Target Top-10 appearances divided by target plus locked business-competitor Top-10 appearances.
items.principle: Top-10 share shows whether the business is a consistent option, not a one-query exception.
items.recommendedIntervention: Compare service by service. A market-wide average can hide a single-service collapse.

items.title: Maps share of visibility

anchors.1: The target earns at least 25% of business-competitor Maps appearances.
anchors.0: The target earns less than 25%.

items.evidence: Target Maps appearances divided by target plus business-competitor Maps appearances.
items.principle: Maps share isolates the local surface from organic and AI.
items.recommendedIntervention: If Maps share is weak, investigate proximity and local relevance before content.

items.title: Organic share of visibility

anchors.1: The target earns at least 20% of business-competitor organic appearances.
anchors.0: The target earns less than 20%.

items.evidence: Target organic appearances divided by target plus business-competitor organic appearances.
items.principle: Organic share isolates search-result visibility from Maps and AI.
items.recommendedIntervention: If organic share is weak, investigate page-to-intent coverage and authority.

items.title: AI recommendation share

anchors.1: The target earns at least 20% of business-competitor recommendations in validated AI answers.
anchors.0: The target earns less than 20%.

items.evidence: Target AI recommendations divided by target plus business-competitor recommendations.
items.principle: AI share shows whether recommendation behavior is concentrated or shared.
items.recommendedIntervention: Compare the cited sources. AI recommendations often follow corroboration, not direct optimization.

items.title: Service-specific competitor gap

anchors.2: The target meets or beats the cohort median top-10 share in at least 75% of core service clusters.
anchors.1: The target meets the median in 40–74% of clusters.
anchors.0: The target meets the median in fewer than 40% of clusters.

items.evidence: Per-service comparison against the locked business-competitor cohort median.
items.principle: Aggregate share can hide a service where the business is structurally behind.
items.recommendedIntervention: Prioritize the clusters where the gap is largest and the service matters commercially.

items.title: Geographic competitor gap

anchors.1: The target meets or beats the cohort median top-10 Maps coverage in at least half of the grid quadrants.
anchors.0: The target meets the median in fewer than half of the quadrants.

items.evidence: Per-quadrant target coverage compared with the locked cohort median.
items.principle: A competitor can dominate one part of the market while the market average looks acceptable.
items.recommendedIntervention: Use the quadrant comparison to decide whether the gap is geographic or service-specific.

items.title: Relevant referring domains

anchors.2: At least 8 relevant referring domains (local, industry, manufacturer, trade, or association).
anchors.1: 3–7 relevant referring domains.
anchors.0: Fewer than 3 relevant referring domains.

items.evidence: Count of referring domains classified as locally or industrially relevant. Generic low-value directories are excluded.
items.principle: Relevant corroboration matters more than raw link quantity.
items.recommendedIntervention: Pursue a small number of genuinely relevant local, manufacturer, trade, or association sources. Do not buy generic directory links.

items.title: Local source relevance

anchors.2: Multiple current local sources corroborate the business as a local operator.
anchors.1: One meaningful local source, or several low-relevance local directories, corroborate it.
anchors.0: No meaningful local corroboration is observable.

items.evidence: The referring domains, listing sources, and their local relevance. The reviewer classifies source relevance.
items.principle: A local business needs local corroboration, not just links from anywhere.
items.recommendedIntervention: Build relationships with local organizations, publications, and trade sources. Do not treat a generic directory as local proof.

items.title: Industry, manufacturer, and trade sources

anchors.2: At least 4 industry, manufacturer, dealer, trade-association, or trade-publication sources.
anchors.1: 1–3 such sources.
anchors.0: No such sources are observed.

items.evidence: Count of industry and trade sources in the referring-domain and listing observations.
items.principle: Trade-specific corroboration supports both search and AI recommendation.
items.recommendedIntervention: Pursue manufacturer/dealer listings, trade associations, and credible trade publications where the business qualifies.

items.title: External listing and entity consistency

anchors.2: At least 80% of observed external listings agree on name, domain, phone, and service category.
anchors.1: 50–79% agree.
anchors.0: Fewer than 50% agree.

items.evidence: Share of observed listings with consistent name, domain, phone, and service category.
items.principle: Inconsistent entity data weakens both local search and AI entity resolution.
items.recommendedIntervention: Correct the highest-authority inconsistent listings first. Cross-reference GBP Scorecard for the primary profile.

items.title: Competitor authority gap

anchors.1: Relevant referring domains meet or exceed the locked cohort median.
anchors.0: Relevant referring domains are below the cohort median.

items.evidence: Target relevant referring domains compared with the locked business-competitor cohort median.
items.principle: Authority is relative. A number without a local comparison is not actionable.
items.recommendedIntervention: Compare the sources the leading competitors have that the business does not. Prioritize relevance over volume.

items.title: Authority overlap with AI citations

anchors.1: At least 25% of the target's relevant authority domains also appear as citation domains in the observed AI answer ecosystem.
anchors.0: Fewer than 25% overlap.

items.evidence: Overlap between relevant referring domains and the domains cited in validated AI observations.
items.principle: AI answers cite sources. If the business is absent from the sources the market relies on, recommendation visibility is fragile.
items.recommendedIntervention: Prioritize sources that both corroborate the entity and appear in AI citations.

items.title: Surface concentration

anchors.1: The Herfindahl index of visibility appearances across Maps/Pack, organic, and AI is 0.55 or lower.
anchors.0: The Herfindahl index is above 0.55.

items.evidence: Surface HHI computed from target appearances across core surfaces. Lower values indicate more diversified discovery.
items.principle: A business that depends on one surface is fragile even when that surface is strong.
items.recommendedIntervention: Do not weaken a strong surface. Build a second surface as insurance and report the concentration explicitly.

items.title: Service concentration

anchors.1: The Herfindahl index of visibility across core service clusters is 0.50 or lower.
anchors.0: The Herfindahl index is above 0.50.

items.evidence: Service HHI computed from demand-weighted target visibility across service clusters.
items.principle: One-service visibility is a business risk, not only an SEO risk.
items.recommendedIntervention: Decide whether the concentration is intentional. If not, build visibility for the next most important service.

items.title: Geographic concentration

anchors.1: The Herfindahl index of top-10 Maps coverage across the four grid quadrants is 0.50 or lower.
anchors.0: The Herfindahl index is above 0.50.

items.evidence: Geographic HHI computed from top-10 coverage across the four grid quadrants.
items.principle: A business visible in one corner of its market may not be visible across the market it claims.
items.recommendedIntervention: Check whether the concentration matches the service area. If not, investigate proximity and location coverage.

items.title: Branded versus non-branded dependence

anchors.1: Branded appearances are 20% or less of total observed search appearances.
anchors.0: Branded appearances are more than 20% of total appearances.

items.evidence: Share of branded visibility among all observed search appearances. Branded queries are diagnostic and never inflate the core score. Only scored when configuration.branded_diagnostics_enabled is true.
items.principle: Strong branded visibility can mask weak non-branded discovery.
items.recommendedIntervention: Separate branded from non-branded demand in every report. Do not let branded rank inflate the core score.

items.title: Reproducible visibility trend

anchors.1: The current demand-weighted visibility index is within 10% of the prior comparable run, or has improved.
anchors.0: The visibility index has declined by more than 10% against a comparable prior run.

items.evidence: Demand-weighted visibility index compared with a prior run that used a comparable query universe and grid. Only scored when configuration.historical_runs_available is true and a comparable run is supplied.
items.principle: A trend is useful only when the comparison is reproducible.
items.recommendedIntervention: Investigate lost visibility by surface and service. Do not invent a trend when the prior run is not comparable.

caps.label: No qualified non-branded discovery
caps.rationale: If the business has zero qualified presence across every required core non-branded discovery surface, despite sufficient valid evidence, it cannot be discovered for the demand it sells. The score is capped in the Critical band. This is the only V1 cap.

validityGates.label: Artifact schema is valid
validityGates.threshold: The audit validates against the V1 schema and its schema_version is known.

validityGates.label: Target business resolved
validityGates.threshold: business.resolution.resolved is true and match confidence is at least 0.80.

validityGates.label: Query universe locked
validityGates.threshold: query_universe.locked is true, a hash is present, and the hash matches the universe content.

validityGates.label: Market configuration matches the universe
validityGates.threshold: Trade, market name, language, and device match between the audit and the query universe.

validityGates.label: Core query coverage
validityGates.threshold: At least 80% of planned core queries are observed on each required core surface.

validityGates.label: Geo-grid coverage
validityGates.threshold: At least 80% of planned grid points are observed for each configured Maps surface.

validityGates.label: Validated AI surface available
validityGates.threshold: At least one validated AI surface has observations.

validityGates.label: AI repeat completeness
validityGates.threshold: At least 80% of planned prompt-platform-repeat observations are present.

validityGates.label: Competitor cohort locked
validityGates.threshold: competitors.locked is true and at least two business competitors are in the locked cohort.

validityGates.label: Authority data present
validityGates.threshold: At least one referring-domain or external listing observation is present.

validityGates.label: Provider error rate
validityGates.threshold: The recorded provider error rate is at most 0.10.

validityGates.label: No critical source outage
validityGates.threshold: No required core source is recorded as a critical outage.

facts.description: True when the target has at least one qualified top-20 or AI mention on any required core non-branded surface.
True when at least one Maps or Local Pack observation exists.
True when at least one organic observation exists.
True when at least one validated AI observation exists.
True when at least one AI surface is marked validated.
True when every required validity gate passes.

crossScorecard.question: Relevant referring domains and external corroboration
GBP phone, website, booking, or messaging action
Website forms, CTA usability, booking flow
Paid search or Local Services Ads presence
Search Console clicks, calls, leads, revenue
